correctness.rationale: For a positive finite-support invariant measure, the map restricts to a permutation of its support. On two points the only possibilities are identity and transposition. If both beta-transformations transpose, integer digit differences make (gamma+1)/(beta+1) rational, which is incompatible with gamma-1=(m/n)(beta-1), beta irrational, and beta!=gamma. If exactly one transposes, the analogous integer differences force either (gamma-1)/(beta+1) or (gamma+1)/(beta-1) to be rational; coefficient comparison in the irrational beta gives a contradiction. Hence both maps fix both atoms, after which Zhao's exact common fixed-point calculation gives the stated set. All quantifiers and the distinct-base boundary are explicit.
